trial_court: HIGH COURT OF JAMMU & KASHMIR AND LADAKH AT JAMMU CRM(M) No. 356/2022
case_name: Anchal Sharma And Ors vs Ut Of J&K And Anr

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Anchal Sharma and Ors — husband, wife, plaintiff
parties.respondent_defendant: UT of J&K and Anr — respondent

facts_of_case: Petitioners sought quashment of FIR No. 0028/2021 dated 02.03.2021, registered under Sections 279/337/504 IPC against them on the complaint of respondent No.2.

legal_principles.principle: The quashment of FIRs and criminal proceedings can be allowed in exceptional circumstances for furthering the cause of justice, especially in cases where matrimonial disputes involving two families are amicably settled subsequent to registration of the FIR.
legal_principles.held: Although this Court is of the opinion that an FIR and the consequent charge-report culminating from the investigation cannot be generally and in a routine manner allowed to be quashed in exercise of the powers under Section 482 of the Code corresponding to Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 ('BNSS' for short), on the mere ground that the parties have settled their controversy that had become the cause of the occurrence, yet the provisions of Section 320 of the Code corresponding to Section 359 of the BNSS do not restrict the powers of this Court vested in it under Section 528 of BNSS to quash the FIR and the consequent investigation process in exceptional circumstances for furthering the cause of justice especially in cases where the matrimonial disputes involving two families are amicably settled subsequent to registration of the FIR.
cited_cases: B. S. Joshi Vs. State of Haryana; AIR (2003) SC 1386

legal_principles.principle: The power to quash FIRs and criminal proceedings has to be exercised with care and caution, depending on the facts of each case.
legal_principles.held: It has been held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Gopakumar B. Nair Vs. CBI; (2014) 5 SCC 800 that, 'Though quashment of non-compoundable offence under Section 482 Cr. P.C. following settlement between parties would not amount to circumvention of Section 320, but such power has to be exercised with care and caution and would depend on facts of each case.'
cited_cases: Gopakumar B. Nair Vs. CBI; (2014) 5 SCC 800

outcome.final_order: Court quashed the FIR in question by invoking its inherent powers vested under the provisions of Section 482 of the Code.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for quashment of FIR
